transcript.text: f/f freezer keeps icing up bottom drawer wont shut proper, defrosted it 2wks ago already full of ice again. indesit

Ice returning within two weeks after a proper defrost is not normal. The drawer is usually being held out by ice building at the bottom, rather than being the cause itself. The first likely cause is warm, damp room air getting past a freezer door that is not sealing fully. That rapidly turns into ice, particularly around the lower drawer. An automatic defrost fault is the other main possibility, especially if the ice is mainly a thick sheet over the rear inside panel rather than on the freezer floor. 1. Switch off and unplug it. Remove the bottom drawer and check that no food, shelf or drawer is preventing the door from closing.
2. Run a hand around the freezer-door rubber seal, particularly the bottom corners. Look for a split, gap, hardened/warped section, or a section that has pulled away. Also check whether the door looks dropped or loose on its hinges. If the seal is dirty or folded, clean and dry it, ease it back into shape, then fully defrost again before restarting. If the seal is torn, the door has dropped, or it still will not seal, that is the repair route. If the door and seal look sound, tell me whether the returning ice is mainly on the freezer floor/bottom drawer area or as a solid build-up on the rear internal panel. The latter would point more strongly to the defrost system and is normally an engineer repair.

checked the seal. bottom corner of the freezer door seal is split about 5cm and the hinge side bottom bit is flattened. door looks straight not sagging. ice is mostly round the front edge and bottom drawer, thick frost

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
The split and flattened section of freezer-door seal are the likely cause. They will let warm, damp kitchen air in at the bottom/hinge side, which fits the thick frost around the front edge and lower drawer. The door itself can be straight yet still fail to seal properly. The practical repair is to replace the freezer door seal/gasket, then do one complete defrost again so all existing ice is gone before using it normally. A defrost alone will keep being temporary while that seal is damaged. Please send the full Indesit model number so the correct seal can be identified. It is usually on a sticker inside the fridge compartment, commonly on a side wall near the salad drawer. If you cannot reach the label at present, that can wait; avoid trying to chip the ice out with sharp tools.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its IB55532W, read it off the rating plate. whats the seal called to search for, and is it push in or screwed? happy to fit it myself

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
Search for an Indesit freezer door seal, also called a freezer door gasket or door rubber. Use the full rating-plate details when ordering, not just the model text if the supplier asks for a service/product code. I cannot confirm a catalogue match for IB55532W, so do not order purely from a photo or by measurements unless the seller suggests compatibility. Indesit’s official spares service is the safest route; otherwise a local appliance-spares supplier can identify it from the rating plate. Whether it is push-in or screwed varies by door and seal version. Many are a push-fit lip tucked into a channel, while others are retained behind the inner door liner and may involve screws. Do not assume it is glued: inspect the new seal and the edge of the old one first. If it will not pull gently from a corner with the appliance switched off, it is likely a retained type and may need the inner door liner loosened rather than forced. After fitting, fully defrost and dry the freezer before restarting it. The split and flattened hinge-side corner are strong evidence that the seal is the reason frost is returning around the front and preventing the bottom drawer closing. If a correctly fitted new seal still leaves a gap or frost returns quickly, the door/hinge alignment or the door itself will need an engineer to assess.

candidates: Door not sealing properly (seal, hinge alignment or an obstruction) (high)
